reference_machine.note: Every tg_reference_toks value in this file was measured on this machine only. Numbers on other hardware will differ and are not guaranteed.

EXACT.description: Token stream is bit-identical to the project reference. Selecting any EXACT profile cannot change what the model produces; it changes only where expert weights live and how fast they arrive.

REPACK.description: Uses llama.cpp's packed Q4_K GEMM kernels for the CPU MoE weights. Deterministic and thread-independent, but the accumulation order differs, so the greedy token stream diverges from the EXACT reference. Same model, same weights, same quantization, same routing, same active expert count.
REPACK.quality_statement: No measurable quality degradation was observed on the tested English prose, C/C++ code, and Thai perplexity corpora. General quality equivalence is not claimed.

memory_model.note: Measured constant from a 256 MiB cache upward. The fixed 0.938 GiB covers the resident non-expert weights, the KV cache at the stated context, and runtime overhead.
memory_model.vram_note: All profiles offload the non-MoE layers to the GPU and peak between 7.5 and 7.8 GiB of the 8 GiB card. A GPU with less than 8 GiB has not been tested.
memory_model.server_note: The per-profile figures above are the peak working set of a 512-token llama-cli generation from a short prompt - the benchmark configuration, and the one directly comparable to the 13.687 GiB the unmodified runtime uses when measured the same way. A llama-server session handling varied real requests at the same 16384 context settles about 1.95 GiB higher, because it touches the whole expert cache slab and fills far more KV cache. Measured across four profiles it was +1.98, +1.95, +1.91 and +1.95 GiB - constant, and independent of cache size. It plateaus: rounds 2 and 3 of a sustained session differed by 0.01 GiB. Budget profile figure + 1.95 GiB for a server.

common.load_mode_note: The research benchmarks passed `--load-mode mmap -lm none`. `-lm` is an alias for `--load-mode`, so the last occurrence won and the effective mode was always `none`. The single flag `--load-mode none` here is exactly equivalent and is the honest spelling.

profiles.name: TINY_MEMORY_EXACT
profiles.intended_user: Smallest possible RAM footprint. Suitable for a machine that must keep most of its memory for other work, or for running alongside a desktop session with browsers and an IDE open.
profiles.limitations: Slowest of the external profiles. Every expert bundle miss is an SSD read, so throughput depends on NVMe latency; a SATA SSD or a hard disk has not been tested and will be materially slower.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: MIN_MEMORY_EXACT
profiles.intended_user: Low RAM budget with a meaningful speed gain over TINY. A good default for a 16 GiB machine.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: LOW_MEMORY_EXACT
profiles.intended_user: The project's headline low-memory point: over 20 tok/s in under 3.5 GiB of working set, bit-identical output. Recommended starting profile.
profiles.limitations: Same SSD dependence as the other external profiles.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: BALANCED_EXACT
profiles.intended_user: The knee of the memory/throughput curve. Choose this when about 5 GiB of working set is acceptable and bit-identical output is required.
profiles.limitations: Larger caches than this were measured (5120 and 6144 MiB) and are dominated: they cost 1-2 GiB more for throughput inside measurement noise.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: MAX_SPEED_EXACT
profiles.intended_user: Fastest configuration that still produces the bit-identical reference token stream. Requires a machine that can spare roughly 14 GiB of working set.
profiles.limitations: Only the first two MoE layers use external storage; the other 28 are resident, which is where the memory goes. Throughput is capped near 32 tok/s by an upstream vec_dot thread-scaling characteristic that the unmodified resident path shares - more threads do not help this configuration.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: MAX_SPEED_REPACK
profiles.intended_user: Fastest overall. Use when raw throughput matters more than bit-identical reproduction of the reference token stream.
profiles.limitations: Does not use the external expert cache at all, so it has no low-memory story: all 30 CPU MoE layers are resident. Its token stream is NOT bit-identical to the EXACT reference. Quality evidence is perplexity on four corpora plus qualitative real-use inspection; that is not a general equivalence proof.
profiles.guarantees: Deterministic and thread-independent output for a given prompt and seed. No measurable quality degradation on the tested corpora.

profiles.name: LONG_CONTEXT_LOW_RAM_64K
profiles.intended_user: Long-context work (up to 65536 tokens) with RAM still bounded. Requires the ggml-expert-indirection.cpp fix in this repo's patches/ (present as of this commit) - a build from an older checkout of patches/ will silently fall back to unbounded resident memory for layers 30-39. See docs/LONG_CONTEXT.md.
profiles.limitations: Measured with a single run per point, not this project's alternating-build protocol (see docs/LONG_CONTEXT.md) - treat tg_reference_toks as +-10%, not +-8% like the 16384 profiles. No measured server working set for this context; budget the CLI figure plus the usual server overhead until measured. Retrieval correctness was validated at this context specifically with a ~44,000-token needle-in-haystack test, not at the full 65536-token window.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: LONG_CONTEXT_LOW_RAM_128K
profiles.intended_user: Long-context work (up to 131072 tokens) with RAM still bounded. Same requirement and caveats as LONG_CONTEXT_LOW_RAM_64K. See docs/LONG_CONTEXT.md.
profiles.limitations: Same as LONG_CONTEXT_LOW_RAM_64K: single run per point, no measured server working set at this context, retrieval correctness validated at ~44,000 tokens (at -c 65536) rather than at this profile's own full window.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: LONG_CONTEXT_LOW_RAM_256K
profiles.intended_user: The model's full native context (262144, its n_ctx_train - going further needs RoPE extrapolation, out of scope) with RAM still bounded. The recommended long-context starting point. See docs/LONG_CONTEXT.md.
profiles.limitations: Single run per point, not the alternating-build protocol - treat tg_reference_toks as +-10%. Retrieval correctness validated at ~44,000 tokens (at -c 65536), not at the full 262144-token window; that would take on the order of an hour of prompt processing and has not been run. llama-server validated directly at this profile: 4.08s load, five real requests (chat, code, reasoning, ~4000-token document, multi-turn) all completed, clean shutdown, zero stale processes.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

profiles.name: REFERENCE_CONTROL
profiles.intended_user: Not a user profile. The unmodified llama.cpp resident path, used as the comparison baseline in benchmarks.
profiles.limitations: Control only. No external expert cache, no repack.
profiles.guarantees: Bit-identical token stream to the project reference.

rejected_configurations.name: LOW_MEMORY_REPACK
rejected_configurations.reason: Implemented and measured. The packed kernels are worth only +4.7% on the external path against the +30% they give the resident path, which does not justify leaving the EXACT class. See docs/RESEARCH_HISTORY.md entry F3.

rejected_configurations.name: cache 5120 / 6144 MiB
rejected_configurations.reason: Dominated by cache 4096 MiB: throughput inside noise, 1-2 GiB more memory.

rejected_configurations.name: -t 12 on the plain (non-repack) path
rejected_configurations.reason: Dominated by the same configuration at -t 4. The plain vec_dot path does not scale past about 4 threads on this CPU.
